## 415. Set-point orders and the optimum: what an order with a point of enough does beyond what couples in (UE1b)

UE1 contained the free-energy principle as a case and read its agents' preferences as characteristic states: a chooser ranking outcomes by closeness to a set point has a point of enough, unlike a maximizer ([UE1's note](../../development/ue1-fep-bridge/NOTE.md), reading 3, with [its corrections](../../development/ue1-fep-bridge/NOTE-CORRECTIONS.md)). The reading claimed that such a chooser escapes the optimizer's drain, not the commons. UE1b tests it against the optimum law of 05 §7 and the joint excess of 05 §1 ([the kit](../../development/ue1b-set-points/NOTE.md)). Part 2 of the board item, pooled generative models (UE1's item e), had already landed with UE1, as `ChoiceCountCapture.pooled_selectsThrough` and `ChoiceCountCapture.pooled_unchosen_beyond`, so this section is part 1.

**How it stands to active inference.** Active inference casts preferences as prior beliefs over outcomes, highest at the characteristic states (Friston and others 2016). Strictly single-peaked at each observed condition, each peak not depending on the others, they form a nearing order, and the drive of homeostatic reinforcement learning, a norm of the deviations from set points (Keramati and Gutkin 2014), is one. A preference indifferent within a tolerance band around the set point is not nearing: the band is a two-sided aspiration level, to which the plateau's results apply. These correspondences are readings, cited from bibliographic knowledge; no source was fetched for the kit.

**The verdict on reading 3.** It holds in part. Below its set point a nearing order rises, and its optima drain as a maximizer's do. At its set point the class is undriven, and what lies beyond stands where the way of reaching the set point leaves it: lower by the shortfall with the loss, in a balanced step in which the whole gains nothing. Where a step can lose what it takes, the set point alone does not protect what lies beyond (`Topped.nearing_either`), while a term on what lies beyond counted after the set point does (`Topped.counted_after_keeps`). That contrast with rising orders belongs to the plateau, not to the set point: counted after a rising order with room the term changes nothing, and counted after an aspiration level (Simon 1955) it keeps as well. So what protects at a set point is how the choice among equal optima is made, mild optimization's point (Taylor 2016), not modelled here. Joint excess applies as read, for any formations holding their levels, with no choice in the law.

**The rule 9 refactor of Optimum.** The kit first proved the three general laws of the exchange beside `Optimum`'s rising laws, repeating their proofs. Board rule 9 asks a general law to land below its special cases. Optimum's owner is inactive, so the lander decided to land the refactor: the three general laws moved verbatim into `Becoming.Optimum`, and the rising laws became two-line corollaries. No statement of `Optimum` or `RegimeMargin` changed: every declaration type was printed from the landed and the refactored builds and compared, and the moved theorems are alpha-identical to the kit's. The seventeen records bound to `Optimum.lean` were re-pointed: sixteen as bookkeeping, in one line of `_process/architecture/rebinds.jsonl` with no history note, and room-read-off-the-exchange with a history note, its fourth law's declaration list now naming the three general laws.

**The review.** An independent read-only review by a separate AI agent ([REVIEW-UE1b](../../development/ue1b-set-points/REVIEW-UE1b.md)) found the Lean sound and the verdict on reading 3 right, and the corrected wording claiming more than the Lean in six places: 2 errors, 6 overclaims, 8 imprecisions, 3 suggestions. The errors:

- "nothing protects" what lies beyond, refuted by the kit's own `Topped.counted_after_keeps`;
- the three general laws proved beside `Optimum`'s (rule 9).

All 19 findings were taken:

- nearer read by betweenness, so that asymmetric single-peaked preferences count;
- the `settled` family renamed;
- `optima_iff`, `counted_after_keeps_iff` and `Nearing.not_rising` added, with the review's probes as the kit's own witnesses;
- the holding laws freed of any set point;
- the refactor applied and its statements compared;
- the text rewritten to the Lean.

The reviewer's re-check found 18 findings addressed and one suggestion in part, the Lean stronger than reviewed, and five small new points: four docstrings garbled by a rename, a misstatement in the note, "single-peaked" without "strictly", "not rising" without its hypothesis, and the re-points' history lines. All were fixed before landing.

**Readings** [AI reading, D45]. A set point removes the drive of the class beyond what couples in, not the draw. The protection a set point seems to offer is a property of the plateau of ways of reaching it and of how one of them is chosen; an aspiration level shares it. Formations holding a level drain a commons wherever their losses together exceed what renews it, whatever they choose: the most robust part of the verdict.
